On res.partner, add a selection field for account status with options Trial, Active, Suspended, defaulting to Trial. Also add an integer field for support priority level, defaulting to 0. Restrict editing both fields to the Sales Manager security group only — other internal users can read them but not change them.

This round's own NEW focus is ONLY: 'support_priority_field'. (This is only this system's own internal tracking name for what to build this round -- it is NOT a literal field, variable, or method name you must create, and it does not describe the SHAPE of the work either (a label mentioning 'decoration' or 'access' or 'relation' does not mean the work is necessarily a new field/method of that name -- it could just as easily be a view attribute, a removed CSV row, or anything else). Real, confirmed bug found live on a DIFFERENT round of this same task: a prior round whose own focus label was quoted here invented an entire unused field literally named after that label, purely because the label appeared in this sentence, even though the actual requirement needed no such field at all (its own generated comment admitted "this field is not used directly"). Read the ORIGINAL goal text above for what this round literally requires and how to name anything you add; never invent a field/method purely to give this round's own label something to point at.) Add ONLY the code this one constraint strictly requires -- no other fields, methods, onchange logic, or security records, even if they seem helpful or related. Every extra line you add that nothing exercises will be reported as a real, uncovered gap and will fail this round on its own, regardless of code quality. This applies to views_xml too: do NOT add view elements referencing any field that isn't defined by THIS round's own models_py change -- referencing a future constraint's field before it exists is a hard, guaranteed failure, not a style choice. Each one will get its own dedicated round later; adding any of their fields now is a guaranteed failure of THIS round, not a head start. Content for those models belongs entirely to the not-yet-in-scope constraints listed above, not this round.
